title: Americans Use AI to Choose Healthy Snacks, Says Report
paragraphs: Choosing a snack used to be simple. You went to the store and picked something you liked. But according to a new report, more and more Americans are now asking artificial intelligence (AI) to help them choose what to eat.

The report comes from Conagra Brands, a large US food company, which worked with the research firm Circana. They analyzed more than 53 million shopping transactions involving 17,000 snack products in the United States, where snacks bring in $198.2 billion in sales each year.

According to the report, Americans are increasingly turning to AI tools for advice on which snacks to buy. Instead of searching for a particular product, many shoppers ask AI to suggest snacks that meet specific needs, such as those that are high in protein or fiber.

The report also found that people are looking for healthier options. Demand for high-protein foods and snacks that support particular health goals is growing, while sales of traditional snacks, such as cookies and chips, have struggled. According to Bob Nolan, a senior vice president at Conagra, snacks are playing a bigger and more personal role in people's lives. The report also found that Gen Z is driving demand for bolder flavors, such as sweet and spicy combinations.
Other surveys show a similar trend. In one survey by the company Curious Plot, 74% of early adopters of new food trends said they used AI to make decisions about food, up from 55% a year earlier.

However, the Conagra report did not say how many people actually use AI to choose snacks. Trust is also an issue. In another survey, by the agency FoodMinds, only 31% of people said they trusted AI tools to give accurate food and nutrition information.
